seed: Somebody building an icon outline draws it in pieces with the Pen. This walk draws two open runs that meet at a corner, picks both rows, and checks that the command is there at all, that it calls itself Join Paths rather than Turn Into Path, that it welds them into ONE outline of three corners, that one undo puts the two runs back, and that when nothing is near enough the command says so under the canvas instead of going quiet.

steps.note: two open runs drawn with the Pen, meeting at the top corner. They LOOK like the top of a shape and are nothing of the kind: two rows in the layers list, no inside, nothing to fill

THE POINT: before this the row menu over two paths offered nothing at all, because the command only asked whether something still had to be TURNED. It is here now, and it reads 'Join Paths…' rather than 'Turn Into Path…', because neither of these is a shape any more

the question reads 'Join both paths into one?' and says their ends meet so they become one outline, and that undo puts it back. It does NOT say they stop being shapes, because they were not shapes. The button says Join Paths. Nothing has changed yet

THE POINT: one path layer where there were two, three corners, sitting exactly where the two runs were. Compare doc-1-two-runs with doc-4-joined: the picture has not moved. The line under the canvas says it joined and how to put it back
the corner where they met was picked up and pulled, and both runs came with it. Two separate paths could never have done this together
one undo puts the corner back, the second takes the whole join back to two separate runs: joining is ONE step. Compare doc-6-runs-back with doc-1-two-runs

THE OTHER HALF OF THE PROMISE: a run away on its own picked with the first one. The command is still offered, because a row dimmed for being three points out teaches nobody anything. It changes nothing and the line under the canvas names the gap and what to do about it: drag an end onto another
